1716.subject: Physics
1716.text: A projectile has a maximum range of $16 \mathrm{~km}$. At the highest point of its motion, it explodes into two equal masses. One mass drops vertically downwards. The horizontal distance covered by the other mass from the time of explosion is
1716.sol:
Maximum range,
$R_{\max }=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}$
Range is maximum when $\theta=45^{\circ}$ Initial momentum at the highest point
$=m u \cos 45^{\circ}=\frac{m u}{\sqrt{2}}$
After explosion, the projectile breaks into two equal masses. As one mass drops vertically downwards, hence its velocity and momentum is zero in the $x$-direction.
Hence, if $v$ be the velocity of second mass, then according to law of conservation of momentum,
$m u \cos 45^{\circ}=\frac{m}{2} v \quad \therefore \quad v=2 u \cos 45^{\circ}$
Horizontal distance covered from the time of explosion
$\begin{aligned} & =v \times \frac{T}{2}=v \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 u \sin 45^{\circ}}{g} \\ & =2 u \cos 45^{\circ} \times \frac{u \sin 45^{\circ}}{g} \\ & =\frac{u^2}{g} \times \sin 90^{\circ}=\frac{u^2}{g}=16 \mathrm{~km}\end{aligned}$

11092.text: In $∆ ABC$, suppose the radius of the circle opposite to an angle $A$ is denoted by ${r}_{1}$, similarly ${r}_{2} ↔$ angle $B, {r}_{3} ↔$ angle $C .$ If $' r '$ is the radius of inscribed circle then, what is the value of $\dfrac{ab - {r}_{1}{r}_{2}}{{r}_{3}} =$
11092.sol:
We know, ${r}_{1} = \dfrac{∆}{s - a}, {r}_{2} = \dfrac{∆}{s - b}, {r}_{3} = \dfrac{∆}{s - c}$

Then, $ab - {r}_{1}{r}_{2} = ab - \dfrac{{∆}^{2}}{\left(s - a\right)\left(s - b\right)}$

$= ab - \dfrac{s\left(s - a\right)\left(s - b\right)\left(s - c\right)}{\left(s - a\right)\left(s - b\right)}$

$= ab - s\left(s - c\right)$

$= ab - \left(\dfrac{a + b + c}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{a + b - c}{2}\right)$

$= \dfrac{4ab - {\left(a + b\right)}^{2} + {c}^{2}}{4}$

$= \dfrac{{c}^{2} - {\left(a - b\right)}^{2}}{4}$

$= \dfrac{c + a - b}{2} \times \dfrac{c - a + b}{2}$

$= \left(s - b\right)\left(s - a\right)$

Now, $\dfrac{ab - {r}_{1}{r}_{2}}{{r}_{3}} = \dfrac{\left(s - b\right)\left(s - a\right)}{\dfrac{∆}{\left(s - c\right)}}$

$= \dfrac{s\left(s - a\right)\left(s - b\right)\left(s - c\right)}{s ∆}$

$= \dfrac{∆}{s}$

$= r$

12018.subject: Mathematics
12018.text: The distance of the point $\left(1, 2\right)$ from the line $x + y + 5 = 0$ measured along the line parallel to $3x - y = 7$& is equal to
12018.sol:
Let the equation of the line parallel to $3x - y = 7$~be $3x - y = \lambda$.

Since, it passes through $\left(1, 2\right)$, this point will satisfy the equation~$3x - y = \lambda$.

$∴ 3 - 2 = \lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

So, the line is $3x - y = 1$.

Now,~$\left(x + y + 5\right) + \left(3x - y\right) = 0 + 1 ⇒ 4x = - 4 ⇒ x = - 1$.

Putting in~$x + y + 5 = 0,$~we get

$y = - x - 5 = 1 - 5 = - 4$

So, the point of intersection of~$x + y + 5 = 0$~and $3x - y = 1$~is $\left(- 1, - 4\right)$.

The required distance is the distance between~$\left(1, 2\right) and \left(- 1, - 4\right).

By distance formula,

the required distance~$= \sqrt{$\left\{1 - \left(- 1\right)$\right\}2 + $\left\{2 - \left(- 4\right)\right\}2}= \sqrt{\left(2\right)2 + \left(6\right)2} = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40}$.

14051.text: Five current carrying conductors meet at a point $P$. What is the magnitude and direction of the current in the fifth conductor?
14051.sol:
Using Kirchoff's junction law which is based upon the law of conservation of charge,

Net charge accumulation at any junction is zero, therefore, $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n} = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + \ldots \ldots + {I}_{n}$

At junction~$P,$

$\left(+ 5A\right) + \left(+ 4A\right) + \left(- 3A\right) + \left(- 5A\right) + {I}_{P} = 0 ⇒ {I}_{P} = 1A$

Therefore, the current of~$1A$is flowing from~$P\text{to}Q .$&

Dividing Eqs. (i) and (ii)

A ball is dropped from a tower of height $80 \mathrm{ m}$. The time it takes to cover the last $50 \%$ of its fall is

The given situation is shown below
For Ist part of journey, $\begin{aligned} & u=0, a=-g=-10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2} \\ & s=-40 \mathrm{ m}\end{aligned}$ Now using, $v^2-u^2=2 a s$ we get, $\quad v^2-0=2 \times(-10)(-40)\Rightarrow \quad v^2=800$...(i) And using $v=u+a t$, we get; $\quad v=0+a t_1$, or $\quad v^2=a^2 t_1^2\Rightarrow \quad t_1^2=\frac{v^2}{a^2}=\frac{800}{100}=8 \Rightarrow t_1=2 \sqrt{2}$ Now, for second part of journey, $u=0, a=-10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2, s=-80 \mathrm{ m}\Rightarrow v^2-u^2=2 a s \Rightarrow v^2=2 \times(-10)(-80)=1600 And \quad v=u+a t_2$ gives, $v=a t_2 \Rightarrow v^2=a^2 t_2^2$ Hence, $1600=100 \times t_2^2$ or $\quad t_2=4 \mathrm{ s}$ Time to complete last $50 \%$ part of the journey $=t_2-t_1=4-2 \sqrt{2} \simeq 1.17 \mathrm{ s}$

19505.subject: Chemistry
19505.text: Identify the end-product [D] formed when solution salicylate undergoes the following series of reactions
19505.sol:
The starting material (A) is sodium salicylate. Treatment with NaOH/CaO/Heat is a decarboxylation reaction (soda-lime decarboxylation), which removes the -COONa group and replaces it with a hydrogen atom. Subsequent treatment with HCl(aq) protonates the phenoxide ion to form phenol. Thus, (B) is phenol.

The reaction of phenol with NaOH(aq) converts it back to sodium phenoxide, which is also labeled as (B) in the reaction scheme. This is a nucleophilic species.

The final step involves the reaction of sodium phenoxide with allyl bromide (CH_2=CH-CH_2Br$). This is a Williamson ether synthesis where the phenoxide oxygen acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of the allyl bromide, displacing the bromide ion. This results in the formation of allyl phenyl ether, which is $C_6H_5-O-CH_2-CH=CH_2$.

Answer: $

19565.subject: Chemistry
19565.text: A Carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ when reacted with Methyl magnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis gave product $\mathrm{Y}$. When $\mathrm{Y}$ is heated with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{ K}$, it gave $\mathrm{Z}$ (2- Methylbut-2-ene) as one of the products. Identify $\mathrm{X}$.
19565.sol:
The reaction of a carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields an alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$.

Heating alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{ K}$ is a dehydrogenation reaction for primary and secondary alcohols, or a dehydration reaction for tertiary alcohols. Since the product $\mathrm{Z}$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is an alkene, the reaction is a dehydration of a tertiary alcohol.

The structure of 2-methylbut-2-ene is $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The tertiary alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ that dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ (2-methylbutan-2-ol) is formed by the reaction of a ketone with methylmagnesium bromide. Specifically, the reaction of butan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$) with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

Therefore, the carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ is butan-2-one.

Answer: Butanone

19856.text: Which of the following factors is altered by the addition of a catalyst during a chemical reaction?
19856.sol:
A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

Thermodynamic state functions such as entropy, enthalpy, and internal energy depend only on the initial and final states of the system (reactants and products) and are independent of the path taken. Therefore, they remain unaffected by the addition of a catalyst.

Answer: Activation energy

20002.text:
Based on Crystal Field theory, match the Complex ions listed in Column I with the electronic configuration in the d orbitals of the central metal ion listed in Column II.
No.ComplexNo.d orbital configuration of central metal ion
A$[Mn(CN)_6]^{4-}$P$e_g^2 t_{2g}^3$
B$[Co(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$Q$t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$
C$[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$R$t_{2g}^5$
D$[MnCl_4]^{2-}$S$t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$
20002.sol:
For $\left[Mn(CN)_6\right]^{4-}$, the oxidation state of $Mn$ is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $Mn^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. Since $CN^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, pairing occurs. The configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$, which is represented by (R).

For $\left[Co(H_2O)_6\right]^{2+}$, the oxidation state of $Co$ is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $Co^{2+}$ is $3d^7$. Since $H_2O$ is a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$, which is represented by (S).

For $\left[Fe(H_2O)_6\right]^{2+}$, the oxidation state of $Fe$ is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $Fe^{2+}$ is $3d^6$. Since $H_2O$ is a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, which is represented by (Q).

For $\left[MnCl_4\right]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of $Mn$ is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $Mn^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. This is a tetrahedral complex with a weak field ligand $Cl^{-}$, so the configuration is $e_g^2 t_{2g}^3$, which is represented by (P).

Comparing these results: $A=R$, $B=S$, $C=Q$, $D=P$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{P}$

20799.text: Which of the following series of transitions in the spectrum of hydrogen atom fall in visible region?
20799.sol:
The wavelength of light emitted during electronic transitions in a hydrogen atom is given by the Rydberg formula: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right), where $ n_1$ is the lower energy level and $n_2$ is the higher energy level.

The Lyman series corresponds to transitions ending at $n_1 = 1$, which fall in the ultraviolet region.

The Balmer series corresponds to transitions ending at $n_1 = 2$, which fall in the visible region.

The Paschen series corresponds to transitions ending at $n_1 = 3$, which fall in the infrared region.

The Brackett series corresponds to transitions ending at $n_1 = 4$, which fall in the infrared region.

Therefore, the Balmer series is the only one among the given options that falls in the visible region.

Answer: Balmer series$

21043.subject: Mathematics
21043.sol:
Let $f(n) = 2^{3n} - 7n - 1 = 8^n - 7n - 1$.

For $n = 1$, $f(1) = 8^1 - 7(1) - 1 = 8 - 8 = 0$, which is divisible by any integer.

For $n = 2$, $f(2) = 8^2 - 7(2) - 1 = 64 - 14 - 1 = 49$.

For $n = 3$, $f(3) = 8^3 - 7(3) - 1 = 512 - 21 - 1 = 490$.

Since $f(2) = 49$ and $f(3) = 490 = 10 \times 49$, the expression $2^{3n} - 7n - 1$ is divisible by 49 for all $n \ge 1$.

Using the binomial expansion, $8^n = (1 + 7)^n = 1 + ^{n}C_{1}(7) + ^{n}C_{2}(7^2) + ^{n}C_{3}(7^3) + \dots + ^{n}C_{n}(7^n)$.

Substituting this into the expression: $f(n) = (1 + 7n + ^{n}C_{2}(49) + ^{n}C_{3}(343) + \dots) - 7n - 1 = ^{n}C_{2}(49) + ^{n}C_{3}(7^3) + \dots$.

Every term in the expansion is a multiple of 49, therefore $f(n)$ is divisible by 49.

Answer: 49

21571.subject: Mathematics
21571.sol:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{x}{2(1+x)^{3/2}} dx$.

Substitute $u = 1+x$, so $du = dx$ and $x = u-1$.

Substituting these into the integral:

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \int \dfrac{u-1}{u^{3/2}} du = \dfrac{1}{2} \int (u^{-1/2} - u^{-3/2}) du$.

Integrating with respect to $u$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{u^{1/2}}{1/2} - \dfrac{u^{-1/2}}{-1/2} \right] + C = \dfrac{1}{2} [2\sqrt{u} + 2\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u}}] + C = \sqrt{u} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u}} + C$.

Substituting $u = 1+x$ back:

$I = \sqrt{1+x} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+x}} + C = \dfrac{1+x+1}{\sqrt{1+x}} + C = \dfrac{2+x}{\sqrt{1+x}} + C$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2+x}{\sqrt{1+x}}+C$

21880.subject: Mathematics
21880.text: A and B play a game where each is asked to select a number from 1 to 25. If the two numbers match, both will win a prize. The probability that they will NOT win a prize in a single trial is
21880.sol:
The total number of possible outcomes when A and B each select a number from 1 to 25 is $25 \times 25 = 625$.

The number of favorable outcomes where they select the same number is 25, which are (1,1), (2,2), ..., (25,25).

The probability that they win a prize is $P(\text{win}) = \dfrac{25}{625} = \dfrac{1}{25}$.

The probability that they will NOT win a prize is $P(\text{not win}) = 1 - P(\text{win}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{24}{25}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{24}{25}$

22939.text: An ideal gas has molar specific heat $\dfrac{5R}{2} at constant pressure. If 1662 J of heat brings about 50 K temperature change, the number of moles of gas is$
22939.sol:
Given the molar specific heat at constant pressure, $C_p = \dfrac{5R}{2}$

The heat supplied at constant pressure is given by:

$Q = n C_p \Delta T$

Substituting the given values (Q = 1662$ J, \Delta T = 50$ K, and $R = 8.31$ J mol^{-1}$ K^{-1}$):

$1662 = n \left(\dfrac{5 \times 8.31}{2}\right) \times 50$

$1662 = n \times 125 \times 8.31$

$1662 = n \times 1038.75$

$n = \dfrac{1662}{1038.75} = 1.6$

Answer: $1.6$

22999.subject: Physics
22999.text: The current through the circular coil is halved and the radius of the coil is doubled. If $B_1$ and $B_2$ are respectively the initial and final magnetic field strength, then:
22999.sol:
The magnetic field at the center of a circular coil is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

Initial magnetic field is $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

The current is halved, so $I' = \dfrac{I}{2}$.

The radius is doubled, so $R' = 2R$.

Final magnetic field is $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I'}{2R'} = \dfrac{\mu_0 \left(\dfrac{I}{2}\right)}{2(2R)} = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\right).$

Therefore, $B_2 = \dfrac{B_1}{4}.$

Answer: $B_2 = \dfrac{B_1}{4}$

Even when each American man is seated adjacent to his wife.
Again

$\begin{aligned}$n(E) & =(5 !) $\times($2 !)^4 \\
P$\left(\frac{A}{E}\right)$& =$\frac{n(A \cap E)}{n(E)}$\\
& =$\frac{(4 !) \times(2 !)^5}{(5 !) \times(2 !)^4}=\frac{2}{5}
\end{aligned}

\Rightarrow \quad$P$\left(\frac{A}{E}\right)=\frac{n(A \cap E)}{n(E)}$ALITER
Fixing four American couples and one Indian man in between any two couples, we have 5 different ways in which his wife can be seated, of which 2 cases are favourable. $\therefore$ Required probability $=\frac{2}{5}$.

29034.subject: Chemistry
29034.text: Which of the following sets includes all the species that will change the orange colour of $K_2Cr_2O_7$ in acidic medium?
29034.sol:
$K_2Cr_2O_7$ in acidic medium acts as a strong oxidizing agent. It changes its colour from orange ($Cr_2O_7^{2-}$) to green ($Cr^{3+}$) when it reacts with a reducing agent.

We need to identify the set in which all species can act as reducing agents (i.e., they can be oxidized to a higher oxidation state).

In option (A), $Fe^{2+}$ oxidizes to $Fe^{3+}$, $Sn^{2+}$ oxidizes to $Sn^{4+}$, $I^-$ oxidizes to $I_2$, and $S^{2-}$ oxidizes to $S$. All of these are reducing agents.

In option (B), $Fe^{3+}$ is already in its maximum stable oxidation state and cannot be oxidized further.

In option (C), $Sn^{4+}$ cannot be oxidized further.

In option (D), $Fe^{3+}$, $SO_4^{2-}$, and $Sn^{4+}$ cannot be oxidized further.

Thus, only the species in option (A) will change the orange colour of $K_2Cr_2O_7$.

Answer: $Fe^{2+}, Sn^{2+}, I^-, S^{2-}$

31639.subject: Chemistry
31639.text: $19.5$ g of fluoro acetic acid (molar mass $= 78$ g mol$^{-1}$) is dissolved in $500$ g of water at $298$ K. The depression in the freezing point of water was $1°$C. What is $K_a$ of fluoro acetic acid? (For water, $K_f = 1.86$ K kg mol$^{-1}$). Assume molarity and molality to have same values.
31639.sol:
The molality of the solution is given by:

$m = \dfrac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Molar mass of solute} \times \text{Mass of solvent in kg}}$

$m = \dfrac{19.5}{78 \times 0.5} = 0.5 \text{ mol kg}^{-1}$

The depression in freezing point is given by:

$\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m$

Substituting the given values:

$1 = i \times 1.86 \times 0.5$

$1 = i \times 0.93$

$i = \dfrac{1}{0.93} = \dfrac{100}{93}$

For the dissociation of a weak acid $HA \rightleftharpoons H^+ + A^-$, the van 't Hoff factor is $i = 1 + \alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the degree of dissociation.

$1 + \alpha = \dfrac{100}{93}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{100}{93} - 1 = \dfrac{7}{93}$

The acid dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by:

$K_a = \dfrac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

Since molarity and molality have the same values, $C = 0.5 \text{ M}$.

$K_a = \dfrac{0.5 \times \left(\dfrac{7}{93}\right)^2}{1 - \dfrac{7}{93}}$

$K_a = \dfrac{0.5 \times \dfrac{49}{93^2}}{\dfrac{86}{93}} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 49}{93 \times 86}$

$K_a = \dfrac{24.5}{7998} \approx 3.06 \times 10^{-3}$

The closest value is $3 \times 10^{-3}$.

Answer: $3 \times 10^{-3}$

32955.text: If the curves, ${x}^{2} - 6x + {y}^{2} + 8 = 0$ and ${x}^{2} - 8y + {y}^{2} + 16 - k = 0, \left(k > 0\right)$ touch each other at a point, then the largest value of $k$ is ____________.

If general equation of circle is ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ then its center is $\left(- g, - f\right)$ and radius is $\sqrt{{g}^{2} + {f}^{2} - c}$

Distance between ${C}_{2}$\left(3, 0\right)and{C}_{1}\left(0, 4\right) is either $\sqrt{k} + 1or$\left|\sqrt{k} - 1\right|$

${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = \sqrt{{\left(3 - 0\right)}^{2} + {\left(0 - 4\right)}^{2}} = 5$

$⇒ \sqrt{k} + 1 = 5$or $\left|\sqrt{k} + 1\right| = 5$

$⇒ k = 16 or k = 36$

$⇒$ Maximum value of $k$ is $36$.

37385.text: The number of relations, defined on the set $\{\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{d}\}$, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is equal to:
37385.sol:
For a set with $n = 4$ elements, reflexive condition requires all diagonal pairs $(a,a), (b,b), (c,c), (d,d)$ to be included.
For symmetric relations, non-diagonal pairs come in symmetric pairs. Number of such pairs = $\binom{4}{2} = 6$.
For each pair, we either include both elements or exclude both → 2 choices each.
Total reflexive and symmetric relations = $2^6 = 64$.

37542.subject: Mathematics
37542.text: Let the mean and variance of $12$ observations be $\dfrac{9}{2}$ and $4$ respectively. Later on, it was observed that two observations were considered as $9$ and $10$ instead of $7$ and $14$ respectively. If the correct variance is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are coprime, then $m + n$ are coprime, then $m + n$ is equal to
37542.sol:
Given,

The mean and variance of $12$ observations be $\dfrac{9}{2}$ and $4$ respectively,

So, mean will be,

$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + \ldots \ldots + 9 + 10 + \ldots . . + {x}_{12}}{12} = \dfrac{9}{2}$

$⇒ {x}_{1} + {x}_{2} \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12} + 19 = 54$

Now removing the observation $9 \text{ and } 10$ and adding the observation $7 \text{ and } 14$,

So, the new total sum of the observation will be,

${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12} + 7 + 14 = 54 - 19 + 7 + 14$

Now new mean will be,

$\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + \ldots . + {x}_{12} + 7 + 14}{12} = \dfrac{56}{12}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x}\text{new} = \dfrac{14}{3}$
Now using the formula of the variance we get,

$\dfrac{{x}_{1}^{2} + {x}_{2}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12}^{2} + {9}^{2} + {10}^{2}}{12} - {\left(\dfrac{9}{2}\right)}^{2} = 4$

$⇒ {x}_{1}^{2} + {x}_{2}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12}^{2} + {9}^{2} + {10}^{2} - 81 \times 3 = 4 \times 12$

$⇒ {x}_{1}^{2} + {x}_{2}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12}^{2} + {9}^{2} + {10}^{2} = 291$

Now removing ${9}^{2} \text{ and } {10}^{2}$ and adding ${7}^{2} \text{ and } {14}^{2}$ we get,

$⇒ {x}_{1}^{2} + {x}_{2}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + {x}_{12}^{2} + {7}^{2} + {14}^{2} = 355$
New variance $= \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{N} - ( \overset{¯}{x}{)}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{355}{12} - {\left(\dfrac{14}{3}\right)}^{2}$
$= \dfrac{281}{36}$

Now on comparing with $\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{281}{36}$ we get,

$⇒ m = 281$ and $n = 36$

$∴ m + n = 317$

38537.text: The sum of all values of $\alpha$, for which the points whose position vectors are $\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar, is equal to
38537.sol:
Let the given vectors be $\overset{\to}{A} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{B} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{C} = \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}and\overset{\to}{D} = 9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

We know that if the vectors are coplanar then $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{AB} & \overset{\to}{AC} & \overset{\to}{AD}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} = \left(\left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AD} = \left(9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 8\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 6\right)\overset{^}{j} + 3k$

Now,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & - 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2 & - 1 \\ 8 & \alpha - 6 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(6 + \alpha - 6\right) + \left(3\alpha + 8\right) + \left({\alpha}^{2} - 6\alpha - 16\right) = 0$

On Simplifying we get,

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} - 2\alpha - 8 = 0$

Therefore, sum of the roots is $- \left(- 2\right) = 2$.

42860.text: Refer the figure given below. $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are refractive indices of air and lens material. The height of image will be _______ cm.
42860.sol:
Taking the pole $P$ as the origin and the direction of incident light as positive:
$\mu_1 = 1$ (air), $\mu_2 = 1.5$ (lens)
$u = -40\text{ cm}$
$R = -20\text{ cm}$ (centre of curvature lies to the left of $P$)
$h_o = +2\text{ cm}$

Using the formula for refraction at a single spherical surface:
$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu_1}{u} = \dfrac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-40} = \dfrac{1.5 - 1}{-20}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} + \dfrac{1}{40} = -\dfrac{1}{40}$

$\dfrac{1.5}{v} = -\dfrac{2}{40} = -\dfrac{1}{20}$

$v = -30\text{ cm}$

The negative sign indicates a virtual image formed $30\text{ cm}$ to the left of $P$.

The transverse magnification for refraction at a spherical surface is:
$m = \dfrac{\mu_1 \cdot v}{\mu_2 \cdot u} = \dfrac{1 \cdot (-30)}{1.5 \cdot (-40)} = \dfrac{-30}{-60} = 0.5$

Therefore:
$h_i = m \cdot h_o = 0.5 \times 2 = 1\text{ cm}$

Hence, the correct option is $(1)\ 1$.

44270.subject: Physics
44270.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a laser light of $560nm$ produces an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of $7 . 2mm$. Now another light is used to produce an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of $8 . 1mm$. The wavelength of second light is _____ $nm .$
44270.sol:
Given here: ${\lambda}_{1} = 560 \times {10}^{- 9}m$, ${\beta}_{1} = 7 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m$ and ${\beta}_{2} = 8 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}m$.

Let $d$ be the width and $D$ be the distance between slit and screen then fringe width, $\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$.

Thus, from above, $\beta ∝ \lambda$

So, the wavelength of second light is ${\lambda}_{2} = \dfrac{{\beta}_{2}}{{\beta}_{1}}{\lambda}_{1} = \dfrac{9}{8}{\lambda}_{1}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{2} = \dfrac{9}{8} \times 560 = 630nm .$

46069.text: In the given figure, the capacitors $C_1, C_3, C_4, C_5$ have a capacitance $4 \mu \mathrm{F}$ each. If the capacitor $C_2$ has a capacitance $10 \mu \mathrm{F}$, then effective capacitance between $A$ and $B$ will be

When a battery is applied across $A and B$, then the points $b and c$ will be at the same potential
$\left(\because C_1=C_4=C_3=C_5=4 \mu \mathrm{F}\right)$
Therefore, no charge flows through $\mathrm{C}_2$. $\mathrm{As}, C_1$ and C_5 are in series.
$\therefore$ Their equivalent capacitance,
$C^{\prime}=\frac{C_1 \times C_5}{C_1+C_5}=\frac{4 \times 4}{4+4}=2 \mu \mathrm{F}$
Similarly, $C_4 and C_3$ are in series. Therefore, their equivalent capacitance
$C^{\prime \prime}=\frac{C_3 \times C_4}{C_3+C_4}=\frac{4 \times 4}{4+4}=2 \mu \mathrm{F}$
Now, $C^{\prime}$ and $C^{\prime \prime}$ are in parallel. Therefore, effective capacitance between A and $B =C^{\prime}+C^{\prime \prime}=2+2=4 \mu \mathrm{F}$

55448.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A) $\alpha$ - amino acids present in protein is L- amino acid.
B) Amino acids contain $\text{NH}_2$ as well as COOH group.
C) Number of amino group and carboxylic group are same in amino acids always.
D) Tryosine was firstly obtained from cheese.
Choose the correct alternatives from below:
55448.sol:
Statement A is correct. Naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids present in proteins have the L-configuration.

Statement B is correct. Amino acids are organic compounds containing both an amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$) and a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$).

Statement C is incorrect. The number of amino and carboxylic groups can vary. Acidic amino acids have more carboxylic groups than amino groups, whereas basic amino acids have more amino groups than carboxylic groups.

Statement D is correct. Tyrosine was first isolated from casein, a protein found in cheese. Its name is derived from the Greek word 'tyros', meaning cheese.

Therefore, statements A, B, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B and D only

56015.subject: Chemistry
56015.text: A first order reaction complete $60$% in $20$ minutes. How long will the reaction take to complete $84$%?
56015.sol:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left(\dfrac{a}{a-x}\right)

For 60\%$ completion in $20$ minutes:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{20} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100-60}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{20} \log(2.5)$

For $84\%$ completion in time $t$:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log\left(\dfrac{100}{100-84}\right) = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log(6.25)$

Equating the two expressions for $k$:

$\dfrac{1}{20} \log$($2.5) = \dfrac{1}{t} \log(2.5^2)$

$\dfrac{1}{20} \log$($2.5) = \dfrac{2}{t} \log(2.5)$

$t = 40$ min

Answer: $40$ min

56038.subject: Chemistry
56038.text: The rate constant of a first order reaction is $1.15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. How long will 5 g of reactant take to reduce to 3 g ?
56038.sol:
The integrated rate law for a first-order reaction is: $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}$.

Given $k = 1.15 \times 10^{-3} \, \texts^{-1}$, $[A]_0 = 5 \, \text{g}$, and $[A]_t = 3 \, \text{g}$, substitute into the formula to obtain:
$t = \frac{2.303}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} \log \left(\frac{5}{3}\right).

The ratio \frac{5}{3} \approx1.6667$, and $\log$(1.6667) \approx$0.2218$. With this, the expression becomes:
$t = \frac{2.303 \cdot 0.2218}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{0.5108}{0.00115} \approx444 \, \text{s}.$

Matching the result with the options, the correct choice is D.

56866.subject: Chemistry
56866.text: If $\mathrm{E}^{{}^{\circ}}\left(\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)=-0.44 \mathrm{ V}$ and $\mathrm{E}^{{}^{\circ}}\left(\mathrm{Sn}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \mid \operatorname{Sn}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)=-0 \cdot 14 \mathrm{ V}$. What is standard emf of cell containing the two electrodes?
56866.sol:
The standard cell EMF is determined from the standard reduction potentials. Tin has the higher (less negative) reduction potential at $-0.14\text{V}$, so it serves as the cathode where reduction occurs: $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Sn}_{(\mathrm{s})}$.

Iron has the lower (more negative) reduction potential at $-0.44\text{V}$, so it serves as the anode where oxidation occurs: $\mathrm{Fe}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2e^-$.

The standard cell potential is calculated as $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{anode}} = (-0.14\text{V}) - (-0.44\text{V}) = +0.30\text{V}$.

Alternatively, using the oxidation potential approach: $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{ox,\mathrm{anode}}} + E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{red,\mathrm{cathode}}} = +0.44\text{V} + (-0.14\text{V}) = +0.30\text{V}$.

The standard EMF of the cell is $+0.30\text{V}$.

$\boxed{\text{A}}$

57975.subject: Chemistry
57975.text: The solubility product of sparingly soluble salt BA is $4 \times 10^{-13}$. Calculate the $[\text{A}^-]$ if $[\text{B}^+]$ is $1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{M}$.
57975.sol:
The dissociation of the sparingly soluble salt $\text{BA}$ is given by:

$\text{BA} \rightleftharpoons \text{B}^+ + \text{A}^-$

The solubility product expression is:

$K_{sp} = [\text{B}^+][\text{A}^-]$

Given:

$K_{sp} = 4 \times 10^{-13}$

$[\text{B}^+] = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{M}$

Substituting the given values into the expression:

$4 \times 10^{-13} = (1 \times 10^{-6}) \times [\text{A}^-]$

$[\text{A}^-] = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-13}}{1 \times 10^{-6}}$

$[\text{A}^-] = 4 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$

Answer: $4 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$

59902.subject: Chemistry
59902.text: Which of the following processes exhibits, $\Delta U = 0$?
59902.sol:
The internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of temperature only.

The change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

In an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, which implies $\Delta T = 0$.

Substituting $\Delta T = 0$ yields $\Delta U = 0$.

Therefore, an isothermal process exhibits $\Delta U = 0$.

Answer: Isothermal process

60563.text: The area of the region bounded by curves $y = \sin x, y = \cos x$ and the lines $x = 0$, $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is
60563.sol:
The required area is given by the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve between the given limits.

In the interval $x \in [0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}]$, $\cos x \ge \sin x$.

Area $= \int_{0}^{\pi/4} (\cos x - \sin x) dx$

$= [\sin x + \cos x]_{0}^{\pi/4}$

$= (\sin \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \cos \dfrac{\pi}{4}) - (\sin 0 + \cos 0)$

$= (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}) - (0 + 1)$

$= \sqrt{2} - 1$

Answer: $\sqrt{2} -$1

61535.subject: Mathematics
61535.text:
The rate of disintegration of a radio active element at time $\mathrm{t}$ is proportional to its
mass at that time. Then the time during which the original mass of $1 \cdot 5 \mathrm{gm}$. will
disintegrate into its mass of $0.5 \mathrm{gm}$. is proportional to
61535.sol:
(C)
Let $m$ be the mass of the radioactive element at time $t$.
Then the rate of disintegration is $\frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}}$ which is proportional to $\mathrm{m}$.
$\therefore \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \mathrm{m} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\mathrm{km}$, where $\mathrm{k} > 0\therefore \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{m}}=-\mathrm{kdt} \Rightarrow \int \frac{1}{\mathrm{ m}} \mathrm{dm}=-\mathrm{k} \int \mathrm{dt}+\mathrm{c}\therefore \log \mathrm{m}=-\mathrm{kt}+\mathrm{c}$
Initially, i.e. when $\mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{ m}=1.5\therefore \log (1.5)=-\mathrm{k} \times 0+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\log \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\therefore \log \mathrm{m}=-\mathrm{kt}+\log \left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \Rightarrow \log \mathrm{m}-\log \frac{3}{2}=-\mathrm{kt}\therefore \log \left(\frac{2 m}{3}\right)=-k t$
When $\mathrm{m}=0.5=\frac{1}{2}$, then
$\begin{aligned}
& \log \left(\frac{2 \times \frac{1}{2}}{3}\right)=-\mathrm{kt} \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)=-\mathrm{kt} \Rightarrow-\log 3=-\mathrm{kt} \\
\therefore & t=\frac{1}{k} \log 3
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Thus required time is proportional to $\log 3$.

63950.text: In triangle ABC, with usual notations, if $(a+b+c)(a+b-c) = ab$, then the measure of angle C is...
63950.sol:
Given $(a+b+c)(a+b-c) = ab$

$((a+b)+c)((a+b)-c) = ab$

$(a+b)^2 - c^2 = ab$

$a^2 + b^2 + 2ab - c^2 = ab$

$a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = -ab$

Using the cosine rule for $\cos C$:

$\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}$

Substituting the value of $a^2 + b^2 - c^2$:

$\cos C = \dfrac{-ab}{2ab} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $0 < C < \pi$, we get $C = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

65619.text: In series LCR resonant circuit, $R=800 \Omega, C=2 \mu F$ and voltage across resistance is 200 V. The angular frequency is $250 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. At resonance, the voltage across the inductance is
65619.sol:
Given: Series LCR circuit with $R = 800 \Omega$, $C = 2 \times 10^{-6}$ F, $V_R = 200$ V at angular frequency $\omega = 250$ rad/s.

At resonance, impedance becomes purely resistive, so the current is $I = \frac{V_R}{R} = \frac{200}{800} = 0.25$ A.

The capacitive reactance is $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{250 \cdot 2 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{1}{5 \times 10^{-4}} = 2000 \Omega$.

Since $X_L = X_C$ at resonance, the inductive reactance is also $2000 \Omega$.

The voltage across the inductance is therefore $V_L = I \cdot X_L = 0.25 \times 2000 = 500$ V.

The voltage across the inductance at resonance is $500$ V.

68441.subject: Physics
68441.text: Spherical insulating ball and a spherical metallic ball of same size and mass are dropped from the same height. Choose the correct statement out of the following {Assume negligible air friction}
options: Time taken by them to reach the earth's surface will be independent of the properties of their materials.
Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.
Both will reach the earth's surface simultaneously.
Metal ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the insulating ball.
68441.sol:
As the metallic ball falls through the Earth's magnetic field, it cuts the magnetic field lines, which induces an electromotive force (EMF) in it.

Since the ball is a conductor, this induced EMF generates eddy currents within the metallic ball.

According to Lenz's law, these eddy currents oppose the motion that causes them, creating an upward magnetic retarding force.

As a result, the net downward acceleration of the metallic ball becomes less than the acceleration due to gravity $g$.

The insulating ball is a non-conductor, so no eddy currents are induced in it. It falls with the full acceleration $g$.

Because the insulating ball has a greater downward acceleration, it will reach the Earth's surface earlier than the metallic ball.

Answer: Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.

71146.subject: Biology
71146.text:
Given below are two statements about vaccines.
Statement (I): Vaccines provide natural acquired active immunity.
Statement (II): The latest hot spot in the field of vaccine research is the development of oral vaccines.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71146.sol:
Statement (I) is incorrect because vaccines provide artificially acquired active immunity, not naturally acquired active immunity. Naturally acquired active immunity is developed when an individual is naturally exposed to a live pathogen and develops a primary immune response.

Statement (II) is incorrect because the latest hot spot in the field of vaccine research is the development of edible vaccines (and DNA/mRNA vaccines), not oral vaccines in general. Oral vaccines, such as the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV), have already been in use for several decades.

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.

71704.subject: Chemistry
71704.text: The bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ ion is:
71704.sol:
The total number of electrons in $\text{N}_2^+$ ion is $14 - 1 = 13$.

The molecular orbital electronic configuration of $\text{N}_2^+$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma^{*}_{2s}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{1}$

Number of bonding electrons, $N_b = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9$
Number of antibonding electrons, $N_a = 2 + 2 = 4$

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2}(9 - 4) = \dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5$

Answer: $2.5$

71935.subject: Chemistry
71935.text: What is the total number of tetrahedral voids present in a single fcc unit cell?
71935.sol:
In an fcc unit cell, the effective number of atoms is $Z = 4$.

The number of tetrahedral voids in a close-packed structure is twice the number of effective atoms.

Number of tetrahedral voids = $2Z = 2 \times 4 = 8$.

Alternatively, in an fcc unit cell, tetrahedral voids are located on the body diagonals. There are $4$ body diagonals and each contains $2$ tetrahedral voids.

Total number of tetrahedral voids = $4 \times 2 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

72006.subject: Chemistry
72006.text: Find the mass of 1 molecule of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in grams.
72006.sol:
Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 98 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of molecules in $1 \text{ mole} = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$

Mass of $1 \text{ molecule} = \dfrac{98}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} \text{ g}$

Mass of $1 \text{ molecule} = 16.27 \times 10^{-23} \text{ g} = 1.627 \times 10^{-22} \text{ g}$

Answer: $1.627 \times 10^{-22}$ g

72025.subject: Chemistry
72025.text: How many total number of s and p electrons are respectively present in $\text{Cl}^-$ ?
72025.sol:
The atomic number of Chlorine ($\text{Cl}$) is $17$.

The $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ion has gained one electron, making the total number of electrons $17 + 1 = 18$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Cl}^{-}$ is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6}$.

Total number of s electrons $= 2 + 2 + 2 = 6$.

Total number of p electrons $= 6 + 6 = 12$.

Answer: $6$ and $12$

72165.subject: Physics
72165.text:
Statement I- When the wavelength of incident radiation in a photoelectric experiment is decreased, then the stopping potential will decrease.
Statement II- In photoelectric effect, if the intensity of light is doubled, then the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons will become double.
options: Statement I is true and statement II is false.
Statement I is false and statement II is true.
72165.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by $K_\max = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of incident radiation and $\Phi$ is the work function.

The stopping potential $V_0$ is related to maximum kinetic energy as $eV_0 = K_\max$.

If the wavelength $\lambda$ is decreased, the term $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$ increases, which increases $K_\max$. Consequently, the stopping potential $V_0$ will increase. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends only on the frequency (or wavelength) of the incident light and the work function of the material. It is independent of the intensity of the incident light. Doubling the intensity increases the number of photoelectrons emitted per second but does not change their maximum kinetic energy. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Both statements are incorrect.

Answer: Both the statements are incorrect.

72220.text: Four point charges $-Q$, $-q$, $2q$ and $3Q$ are placed at corners of the square respectively. The relation between $Q$ and $q$ for which the potential at the centre of the square is zero, is
72220.sol:
Let the side length of the square be $a$. The distance of the centre from each corner is $r = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The electric potential at the centre of the square is the algebraic sum of the potentials due to all four charges.

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{-Q}{r} + \dfrac{-q}{r} + \dfrac{2q}{r} + \dfrac{3Q}{r} \right)

Given that $V = 0$, we have:

$-Q - q + 2q + 3Q = 0$

2Q + q = 0$

$Q = -\dfrac{q}{2}

Answer: $ Q = -q/2

72315.subject: Physics
72315.text:
Identify the equation that DOES NOT represent oscillatory motion.
(A$ is amplitude of motion)$
72315.sol:
Let us analyze each option to determine if it represents oscillatory motion.

For the equation $y = A\sin\omega t + A\cos 2\omega t$, the motion is a superposition of two harmonic functions with commensurable frequencies. This represents a periodic and oscillatory motion.

For the equation $x = A\cos \left(\omega$t - $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right),$ the motion is simple harmonic, which is inherently oscillatory.

For the equationy = A\sin$\omega$t + A\cos($\omega$t + $\pi$/2)$, we can simplify it using the trigonometric identity $\cos($\theta + \pi$/2) = -\sin$\theta:
$y = A\sin$\omega$t - A\sin$\omega$t = 0$
Since the displacement $y$ is zero for all time $t$, the particle remains at rest at the origin. Therefore, this does not represent oscillatory motion.

For the equation $y = A\sin $\left(\omega t - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, the motion is simple harmonic, which is oscillatory.

Thus, the equation that does not represent oscillatory motion is $y = A\sin\omega t + A\cos(\omega t + \pi/2)$.

Answer: $y = A\sin\omega t + A\cos(\omega t + \pi/2)$

72370.subject: Physics
72370.text:
$Below we give four entries for the truth table of two point input OR gate. Which two are wrong?
\begin{array}{cccc} & A & B & Y\\ \text{i} & 1 & 0 & 1\\ \text{ii} & 1 & 1 & 0\\ \text{iii} & 0 & 0 & 1\\ \text{iv} & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}$
72370.sol:
The Boolean expression for an OR gate is $Y = A + B$.

Evaluating each given entry:

For (i): $A = 1, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 1 + 0 = 1$. This is correct.

For (ii): $A = 1, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 1 + 1 = 1$. The given value is $0$, so this is wrong.

For (iii): $A = 0, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 0 + 0 = 0$. The given value is $1$, so this is wrong.

For (iv): $A = 0, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 0 + 1 = 1$. This is correct.

The wrong entries are (ii) and (iii).

Answer: (ii) and (iii)

The circle $x^2+y^2-2 x=0$ is partitioned by line $y=x$ in two segments. Let $\mathrm{A}_1, \mathrm{ A}_2$ be the areas of major and minor segments respectively.
What is the value of $\frac{2\left(A_1+A_2\right)}{A_1-3 A_2}$ ?
76425.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
\text{ Given, } \quad & & x^2+y^2-2 x & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & & (x-1)^2+y^2 & =1 \\
\text{$ or $} & & y^2 & =1-(x-1)^2
\end{aligned}$
Area of minor segment $\left(\mathrm{A}_2\right)\begin{aligned}
& =\int_0^1 \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2-(x)} d x \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{ A}_2 & =\left[\frac{(x-1)}{2} \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(x-1)-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{ A}_2 & =\left[\left(0+\frac{1}{2}(0)-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]-\left[0+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(-1)-0\right] \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{A}_2 & =\frac{\pi-2}{4}
\end{aligned}\frac{2\left(\mathrm{ A}_1+\mathrm{A}_2\right)}{\mathrm{A}_1-3 \mathrm{ A}_2}=\frac{2(\pi)}{\left(\frac{3 \pi+2}{4}\right)-\frac{3(\pi-2)}{4}}=\pi$

77991.subject: Mathematics
77991.text: In an entrance test there are multiple choice questions. There are four options for each question, of which only one is correct. The probability that a student knows the answer to a question is $90\%$. If he gets the correct answer to a question, then what is the probability that he was guessing ?
77991.sol:
Let $E_1$ be the event that the student knows the answer and $E_2$ be the event that the student guesses the answer.

Let $A$ be the event that the student gets the correct answer.

From the given information:
$P(E_1) = \dfrac{90}{100} = \dfrac{9}{10}$
$P(E_2) = 1 - P(E_1) = \dfrac{1}{10}$

If the student knows the answer, the probability of getting it correct is $1$, so $P(A|E_1) = 1$.

If the student guesses, since there are $4$ options with only one correct, $P(A|E_2) = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

The probability that the student was guessing given that the answer is correct is $P(E_2|A)$.

Using Bayes' theorem:
$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{P(E_2) P(A|E_2)}{P(E_1) P(A|E_1) + P(E_2) P(A|E_2)}$

$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{1}{4}}{\dfrac{9}{10} \times 1 + \dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{1}{4}}$

$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{40}}{\dfrac{9}{10} + \dfrac{1}{40}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{40}}{\dfrac{37}{40}} = \dfrac{1}{37}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{37}$

Let $\alpha, \beta$ be two roots then
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & & \alpha^2+\beta_2 & =2 b \text{ (given) } \\

& & & =\frac{-b}{1}=-b \\
\Rightarrow & & \alpha^2+\beta^2 & =(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 b & =k^2-2(-b) \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 b & =k^2+2 b \\
\Rightarrow & k^2 & =0 \Rightarrow k=0 .
\end{array}$

80623.subject: Botany
80623.text:
Identify the correct statements regarding Mass flow hypothesis.
(A) Mass flow is faster than diffusion.
(B) Mass flow is the result of pressure difference between the end points.
(C) Different substances involved in mass flow move at different paces.
(D) Mass flow can result through either a positive or a negative hydrostatic pressure gradient.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
80623.sol:
Long distance transport of substances within a plant cannot be by diffusion alone as it is a slow process. Thus, special long distance transport system (mass flow system) become necessary so as to move substances across long distance and at a much faster rate. Thus statement $(A)$ is correct.
Mass flow is the movement of substances in bulk from one point to another as a result of pressure differences between the two points. Thus, statement $(B)$ is correct.
It is a characteristic of mass flow that substances, whether in solution or in suspension, are swept along at the same pace. Thus, statement $(C)$ is incorrect.
Bulk flow can be achieved either through a positive hydrostatic pressure gradient or a negative hydrostatic pressure gradient. Thus, statement (D) is correct.
Thus, option (2) is correct as it is mentioning all the correct statements.

$\text{K} . \text{E} . = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{m}( {r}^{2} )( \dfrac{8\text{\pi K}}{r} ) = \dfrac{1}{2}mr( 8\piK )$

$8 \times {10}^{- 4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 6.4 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 8 \times 3.14 \times \text{K}$

$K = \dfrac{2}{6.4 \times 3.14} = 0.1m{s}^{- 2}$

84872.text: Unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material was first proposed by
84872.sol:
In 1928, Frederick Griffith, a bacteriologist from Britain, in a series of experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae (bacterium responsible for pneumonia), witnessed miraculous transformation in the bacteria. During the course of his experiment, a living organism (bacteria) had changed in it's physical form.

The unequivocal proof of DNA being the genetic material came from the experiments performed by Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase in the year 1952. They worked with bacteriophages, i.e, the viruses that infect bacteria by using radiolabeled T2 bacteriophages and their and their specific host E.coli cells, they concluded that DNA is the genetic material and not the proteins.

88478.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
88478.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Cassiterite ore of tin contains the impurities of Wol-framite which are separated by electromagnetic separator.
Tin metal is obtained by the carbon reduction of black tin.
In the extraction of lead from galena, the roasting and self-reduction are carried in the same furnace at different temperatures.
Reducing agent of haematite in blast-furnace is coke in upper part and CO in lower part of furnace.
88478.sol:
(i) Cassiterite contains iron and manganese tungstate, called as Wolframite.

They have magnetic properties.

(ii) Purified ore that contains 70% $\text{Sn}{\text{O}_{2}$ is called black tin.

$\text{Sn}{\text{O}_{2} + 2C \to \text{Sn} + 2\text{CO}$ (carbon reduction)

(iii) Roasting is done at moderate temperature in presence of air in reverberatory furnace. Then air supply is stopped and temperature is increased to melt the mass when self

reduction takes place.

(iv) At 500 to 800K (lower temperature range in the upper part of blast furnace)

$3\text{F}{\text{e}_{2}{O}_{3} + CO \to 2\text{F}{\text{e}_{3}{O}_{4} + \text{C}{\text{O}_{2}$

$\text{F}{\text{e}_{3}{O}_{4} + CO \to 3\text{Fe} + 4\text{C}{\text{O}_{2}$

$\text{F}{\text{e}_{2}{O}_{3} + CO \to 2\text{FeO} + \text{C}{\text{O}_{2}$

At 900 to $1500K$ (higher temperature range in the lower part of blast furnace:

$C + \text{C}{\text{O}_{2} \to 2\text{CO}$ , $\text{FeO} + CO \to Fe + \text{C}{\text{O}_{2}$

88749.text:
An aqueous solution of a metal bromide $MB{r}_{2}\left(0 . 05M\right)$ is saturated with ${H}_{2}S .$ What is the minimum pH at which MS will precipitate? ${K}_{sp}$ for $MS = 6 . 0 \times {10}^{- 21} .$ Concentration of saturated ${H}_{2}S = 0 . 1M; {K}_{1} = {10}^{- 7}$ and ${K}_{2} = 1 . 3 \times {10}^{- 13}$ for ${H}_{2}S .$
[Report your answer by rounding it upto nearset whole number]
88749.sol:
For the precipitation of MS form a solution of $MB{r}_{2}$ by passing ${H}_{2}S$
${\text{K}}_{\text{sp}\left(\text{MS}\right)} = \left[{\text{M}}^{2 +}\right]\left[{\text{S}}^{2 -}\right]$
or $6 \times {10}^{- 21} = \left[0 . 05\right]\left[{S}^{2 -}\right]$
or $\left[{S}^{2 -}\right] = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 19}M$
i.e. precipitation of MS will start when ${H}_{2}S$ provides
$1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 19}M{\text{ion of S}}^{2 -}$
For ${\text{H}}_{2} \text{S} ⇌ 2{\text{H}}^{+} + {\text{S}}^{2 -}$
$K = {K}_{1} \times {K}_{2} = \dfrac{{[ {H}^{+} ]}^{2} [ {S}^{2 -} ]}{[ {H}_{2}S ]}$
or ${10}^{- 7} \times 1 . 3 \times {10}^{- 13} = \dfrac{{[ {H}^{+} ]}^{2} [ 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 19} ]}{0 . 1}$
or $\left[{H}^{+}\right] = 1 . 04 \times {10}^{- 1}$
$∴ \text{pH=0.9826}$

88872.text:
Which Of the following orders is correct?

(1) $Sb{H}_{3} > N{H}_{3} > As{H}_{3} > P{H}_{3}$ - Boiling Point

(2) $N{H}_{3} > P{H}_{3} > As{H}_{3} > Sb{H}_{3}$ - Thermal Stability

(3) $N{H}_{3} > P{H}_{3} > As{H}_{3} > Sb{H}_{3}$ - Basic Character

(4) $N{H}_{3} > P{H}_{3} > As{H}_{3} > Sb{H}_{3}$ - Bond Angle
88872.sol:
(1) $\text{N}{\text{H}_{3}$ has higher boiling point than $\text{As}{\text{H}_{3}$ and $\text{P}{\text{H}_{3}$ on account $H$ ‐bonding. $\text{Sb}{\text{H}_{3}$ has highest boiling point on account of highest molecular weight.

(2) As the size of element increases, the strength of M‐H bond decreases and thus stability decreases.

(3) Basicity decreases down the group. (Drago rule).

(4) HEH angle ${(}^{∘}$ ) $: \text{N}{\text{H}_{3} = 107.8; \text{P}{\text{H}_{3} = 93.6, \text{As}{\text{H}_{3} = 91.8; \text{Sb}{\text{H}_{3} = 91.3.$

90949.text: The locus of the mid-points of the chords of the hyperbola $3x^{2} - 2y^{2} + 4x - 6y = 0$ which are parallel to the line $y = 2x + 4$& is
90949.sol:
Let mid-point of the chord is $\left(h, k\right)$
$⇒$ equation of the chord is
$3hx - 2ky + 4\left(\dfrac{x + h}{2}\right) - 6\left(\dfrac{y + k}{2}\right) = 3h^{2} - 2k^{2} + 4h - 6k$
$⇒ \left(3h + 2\right)x + \left(- 2k - 3\right)y = 3h^{2} - 2k^{2} + 2h - 3k$
$⇒$ Slope of the chord is equal to $\dfrac{3h + 2}{2k + 3} = 2$
$⇒$ locus of the mid-points is $3x + 2 = 4y + 6$
$⇒ 3x - 4y - 4 = 0$

91703.text: The sum of all real values of $x$ satisfying the equation ${\left(x^{2} - 5x + 5\right)}^{x^{2} + 4x - 60} = 1$ is
91703.sol:
The given equation will be true in 3 cases.

Case 1: when $x^{2} - 5x + 5 = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} - 5x + 4 = 0$

$⇒ x = 1, 4$

Case 2: when $x^{2} + 4x - 60 = 0$

$⇒ x = 6, - 10$

Case 3: when $x^{2} - 5x + 5 = - 1$ and $x^{2} + 4x - 60 \in$ even integers

Now, $x^{2} - 5x + 5 = - 1$

$⇒ x = 2, 3$

Only $x = 2$ satisfies the given condition,

Hence, sum of all real values of $x$ is $1 + 4 + 6 - 10 + 2= 3$

92991.subject: Physics
92991.text:
As shown in figure, the two parallel conducting rails, in a horizontal plane, are connected at one end by an inductor of inductance$L$. A slider (metallic) of mass $m$, is imparted a velocity ${v}_{0}_{,} upon the rails, as shown in figure. The period of oscillation of the conducting rod is

$
92991.sol:
From energy conservation (there are no dissipative forces)-

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{2} \times 2v\dfrac{dv}{dt} + \dfrac{L}{2} \times 2I\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0$

$mv\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IL\dfrac{dI}{dt}$

The emf induced in an inductor is

$E = L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Blv$

$⇒ L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Bl\dfrac{dx}{dt} ⇒ LdI = Bldx ⇒ I = \dfrac{Bl}{L}x$

The force acting on a current-carrying conductor is

$m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IBl$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \dfrac{IBl}{m}$

Substituting the value of $I$ we get

$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \left(\dfrac{Bl}{L}x\right)\dfrac{Bl}{m} ⇒ a = - \left(\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}\right)x$

We got acceleration in the form of

$a = - {ω}^{2}x$

this implies that the motion is& SHM, with angular frequency

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}}$

The time period of motion is
$⇒ T = 2\pi\dfrac{\sqrt{mL}}{Bl}$

The moment of inertia of the system about instantaneous axis of rotation is given by,

$I = {I}_{ring} + {I}_{rod}$

$⇒ I = ( {MR}^{2} + {MR}^{2} ) + \left(\dfrac{1}{12}{MR}^{2} + {MR}_{1}^{2}\right) & & & (From parallel axis theorem)

$⇒ I = 2{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{12}{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{5}{4}{MR}^{2} = 2{MR}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{3}{MR}^{2} = \dfrac{10}{3}{MR}^{2}$

Hence, ${I}_{system} = \dfrac{10}{3}{MR}^{2}.

Now$ from work - energy theorem, we get,

Mg$\dfrac{R}{2} =Rotational kinetic energy of the system about instantaneous axis of rotation
(here \dfrac{R}{2} is the distance through which the center of mass of the rod descends)

$⇒ Mg$\dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{system}{ω}^{2}$

$⇒ $\omega = $\sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{10R}$}$

Now velocity of center of mass is given as, $v = R $\omega.
$⇒ v = R \times \sqrt{$\dfrac{3g}{10R}}$

100704.subject: Physics
100704.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A box placed on a flatbed truck will slide forward relative to the truck if the truck accelerates forward with an acceleration greater than $\mu_s g$.

Reason (R): The maximum static friction between the box and the truck floor cannot provide an acceleration greater than $\mu_s g$ to the box.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
100704.sol:
Assertion (A) is false. When the truck accelerates forward, the pseudo force on the box acts in the backward direction relative to the truck. If the truck's acceleration exceeds the maximum acceleration that static friction can provide, the box will slide backward, not forward, relative to the truck.

Reason (R) is true. The only horizontal force acting on the box in the ground frame is static friction. The maximum static friction is $f_{s,max} = \mu_s mg$. Therefore, the maximum acceleration it can provide to the box is $a_{max} = \dfrac{\mu_s mg}{m} = \mu_s g$.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

101382.subject: Physics
101382.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a body is taken to a depth $d = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$, its weight becomes half of its weight on the surface, but if it is taken to a height $h = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$, its weight becomes less than half.
Reason (R): For a given distance from the surface of the Earth, the decrease in the value of acceleration due to gravity is always greater inside the Earth than outside it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
101382.sol:
Let $g$ be the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth.

At depth $d = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$, the acceleration due to gravity is $g_d = g\left(1 - \dfrac{d}{R_E}\right) = g\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{g}{2}$. Thus, the weight becomes half.

At height $h = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$, the acceleration due to gravity is $g_h = g\left(\dfrac{R_E}{R_E+h}\right)^2 = g\left(\dfrac{R_E}{R_E + R_E/2}\right)^2 = g\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4g}{9}$. Since $\dfrac{4}{9} < \dfrac{1}{2}$, the weight becomes less than half. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true.

The decrease in $g$ at depth $d = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$ is $\Delta g_{in} = g - \dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{g}{2} = 0.5g$.
The decrease in $g$ at height $h = \dfrac{R_E}{2}$ is $\Delta g_{out} = g - \dfrac{4g}{9} = \dfrac{5g}{9} \approx 0.55g$.
Since $\Delta g_{out} > \Delta g_{in}$, the decrease is greater outside the Earth than inside for the same distance from the surface. Therefore, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

101726.text: A cylindrical tank is filled with water to level of $3 \mathrm{~m}$. A hole is opened at height of $52.5 \mathrm{~cm}$ from bottom. The ratio of the area of the hole to that of cross-sectional area of the cylinder is 0.1 . The square of the speed with which water is coming out from the orifice is (Take $g=10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$ )
101726.sol:
Suppose $A$ be the area of cross section of tank, $a$ be the area of hole, $v_e$ be the velocity of efflux, $h$ be the height of liquid above the hole,
Let $v$ be the speed with which the level decreases in the container. Using equation of continuity, we get $a v_e=A v \quad or \quad v=\frac{a v_e}{A}$ Using Bernoulli's theorem, we have $\begin{aligned} & P_0+h \rho g+\frac{1}{2} \rho v^2=P_0+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_e^2 \\ & h \rho g+\frac{1}{2} \rho\left(\frac{a v_e}{A}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_e^2 \\ & \text{$ or $} \quad v_e^2=\frac{2 h g}{1-\left(a^2 / A^2\right)}=\frac{2 \times(3-0.525) \times 10}{1-(0.1)^2} \\ & \quad=50 \mathrm{~m}^2 \mathrm{~s}^{-2}\end{aligned}$

102909.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a solid spherical conductor of radius $R$ is given a charge $Q$, the magnitude of the electric field at a distance $x$ ($x > 0$) from its surface is $\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(R+x)^2}$.

Reason (R): For calculating the electric field at an external point, the effective distance is measured from the surface of the charged spherical conductor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.
102909.sol:
The electric field at an external point due to a charged spherical conductor is calculated by assuming its entire charge is concentrated at its geometric centre.

If a point is at a distance $x$ from the surface of a sphere of radius $R$, its distance from the centre of the sphere is $r = R + x$.

The electric field is $E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r^2} = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(R+x)^2}$. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The Reason is incorrect because the effective distance for an external point is measured from the centre of the sphere, not from its surface.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.

103523.sol:
Relative permeability is given by $\mu_r = 1 + \chi_m$.

$\mu_r = 1 + 499 = 500$

The magnetic induction $B$ inside the material is given by $B = \mu H = \mu_0 \mu_r H$.

$B = (4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 500 \times 4000$

$B = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 2 \times 10^6 = 0.8\pi$ T

Answer: $0.8\pi$ T

103669.subject: Physics
103669.text:
Two different experimental setups are used to levitate a straight horizontal wire using the magnetic force from a parallel fixed wire directly below it.

In Setup 1, a free wire having mass per unit length $\lambda_1$ carries a current $I$. It is levitated by a fixed wire carrying current $I$ at a distance $d$ below it.

In Setup 2, a free wire having mass per unit length $\lambda_2$ carries a current $2I$. It is levitated by a fixed wire carrying current $3I$ at a distance $2d$ below it.

Assuming both setups are in equilibrium under gravity, the ratio $\lambda_1 : \lambda_2$ is :
103669.sol:
For a wire to be levitated, the upward magnetic force per unit length must balance its downward weight per unit length.

In Setup 1:
$\lambda_1 g = \dfrac{\mu_0 I \times I}{2\pi d} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi d}$

In Setup 2:
$\lambda_2 g = \dfrac{\mu_0 (2I)(3I)}{2\pi (2d)} = \dfrac{6\mu_0 I^2}{4\pi d} = \dfrac{3\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi d}$

Dividing the equation for Setup 1 by the equation for Setup 2:
$\dfrac{\lambda_1 g}{\lambda_2 g} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi d}}{\dfrac{3\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi d}}$

$\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $1 : 3$

104475.subject: Physics
104475.text: A plano-convex lens of refractive index $1.5$ has a radius of curvature of $20\text{ cm}$ for its curved surface. If its plane surface is silvered, what will be the effective focal length of the resulting system?
104475.sol:
The silvered lens acts as an equivalent mirror.

The power of the equivalent mirror is given by:
$P_{eq} = 2P_{l} + P_{m}$

The focal length of the plano-convex lens $f_{l}$ is:
$\dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} - 0\right) = \dfrac{0.5}{20} = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The power of the lens is $P_{l} = \dfrac{1}{f_{l}} = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Since the plane surface is silvered, it acts as a plane mirror with an infinite radius of curvature. Its focal length $f_{m} = \infty$, so its power $P_{m} = 0$.

The equivalent power of the system is:
$P_{eq} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{40}\right) + 0 = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The effective focal length $F$ of the system is:
$F = -\dfrac{1}{P_{eq}} = -20\text{ cm}$

Answer: $-20\text{ cm}$

104501.subject: Physics
104501.text: A plano-convex lens is made of a material with a refractive index of $1.5$. If the radius of curvature of its curved surface is $25\text{ cm}$, what is the power of the lens?
104501.sol:
According to the Lens Maker's formula, the focal length $f$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

For a plano-convex lens, the radius of curvature of the curved surface is $R_1 = +25\text{ cm} = +0.25\text{ m}$, and the plane surface has an infinite radius of curvature, so $R_2 = \infty$.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{0.25} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.5 \times 4 = 2\text{ m}^{-1}$

The power of the lens is $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$ (with $f$ in meters).

Therefore, $P = +2\text{ D}$.

Answer: $+2\text{ D}$

104710.subject: Physics
104710.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the changes made to a standard Young's double slit experiment setup and their effects on the angular fringe width.

List-I (Change in setup)List-II (Effect on angular fringe width)
A. Screen moved away from slitsI. Increases
B. Slit separation is halvedII. Decreases
C. Setup is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.5$III. Remains constant
D. Incident light changed from blue to redIV. Becomes double

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104710.sol:
The angular fringe width in a Young's double slit experiment is given by $\theta = \dfrac{\lambda}{d}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength and $d$ is the slit separation. It is independent of the screen distance $D$.

A. Screen moved away from slits: Since $\theta$ does not depend on $D$, the angular fringe width remains constant. (A $\rightarrow$ III)

B. Slit separation is halved: New slit separation $d' = \dfrac{d}{2}$. The new angular width $\theta' = \dfrac{\lambda}{(d/2)} = 2\left(\dfrac{\lambda}{d}\right) = 2\theta$. It becomes double. (B $\rightarrow$ IV)

C. Setup is immersed in a liquid: The wavelength decreases to $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{1.5}$. Since $\theta \propto \lambda$, the angular fringe width decreases. (C $\rightarrow$ II)

D. Incident light changed from blue to red: The wavelength of red light is greater than that of blue light ($\lambda_{\text{red}} > \lambda_{\text{blue}}$). Since $\theta \propto \lambda$, the angular fringe width increases. (D $\rightarrow$ I)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

105224.subject: Physics
105224.text: An ideal battery of $10\text{ V}$ is connected across two parallel branches. The first branch consists of an ideal p-n junction diode in series with a $5\ \Omega$ resistor, where the p-side of the diode is connected to the positive terminal of the battery. The second branch consists of another ideal p-n junction diode in series with a $10\ \Omega$ resistor, where the n-side of this diode is connected to the positive terminal of the battery. What is the total current supplied by the battery?
105224.sol:
The diode in the first branch has its p-side connected to the positive terminal of the battery, so it is forward biased. Being an ideal diode, it acts as a short circuit and offers zero resistance.

The diode in the second branch has its n-side connected to the positive terminal of the battery, so it is reverse biased. It acts as an open circuit and offers infinite resistance.

Therefore, current only flows through the first branch.

The current $I$ supplied by the battery is given by Ohm's law:
$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\text{ A}$.

Answer: $2\text{ A}$

105543.subject: Physics
105543.text: An isotropic point source emits light of wavelength $\lambda$ at a constant power $P$. A small detector of area $A$ is placed at a distance $r$ from the source, oriented such that the light falls normally on it. Which of the following expressions gives the number of photons striking the detector per second? (Assume $h$ is Planck's constant and $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum)
105543.sol:
The energy of a single photon is given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

The total number of photons emitted by the source per second is $N = \dfrac{P}{E} = \dfrac{P \lambda}{hc}$.

Since the source is isotropic, the emitted photons spread uniformly over a spherical surface area of $4 \pi r^2$ at a distance $r$.

The fraction of these photons intercepted by the detector of area $A$ is $\dfrac{A}{4 \pi r^2}$.

Thus, the number of photons striking the detector per second is $N' = N \times \left(\dfrac{A}{4 \pi r^2}\right) = \dfrac{P \lambda A}{4 \pi r^2 h c}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{P \lambda A}{4 \pi r^2 h c}$

Answer: $3d_{xy}$

107784.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Chemical Species)List-II (Lone pairs on central atom)
(A) $\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$(I) 1
(B) $\text{XeOF}_{4}$(II) 2
(C) $\text{BrF}_{3}$(III) 3
(D) $\text{I}_{3}^{-}$(IV) 0

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
107784.sol:
The number of lone pairs on the central atom can be calculated by subtracting the number of electrons shared in bonds from the total valence electrons (including charge) and dividing by 2.

(A) $\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$: Central S atom has 6 valence electrons + 2 (from negative charge) = 8 available electrons. Four oxygen atoms are divalent and consume $4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons. Remaining electrons = 0. Lone pairs = 0.

(B) $\text{XeOF}_{4}$: Central Xe atom has 8 valence electrons. One oxygen atom consumes 2 electrons and four fluorine atoms consume 4 electrons. Total electrons used = 6. Remaining electrons = $8 - 6 = 2$. Lone pairs = 1.

(C) $\text{BrF}_{3}$: Central Br atom has 7 valence electrons. Three fluorine atoms consume 3 electrons. Remaining electrons = $7 - 3 = 4$. Lone pairs = 2.

(D) $\text{I}_{3}^{-}$: Central I atom has 7 valence electrons + 1 (from negative charge) = 8 available electrons. Two terminal iodine atoms consume 2 electrons. Remaining electrons = $8 - 2 = 6$. Lone pairs = 3.

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

108650.subject: Chemistry
108650.text:
For the synthesis of ammonia by the Haber process,
$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$
What is the correct relationship between the change in enthalpy ($\Delta \text{H}$) and the change in internal energy ($\Delta \text{U}$) at constant temperature?
108650.sol:
For the given reaction:
$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}$) is calculated as:
$\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = (\text{moles of gaseous products}) - (\text{moles of gaseous reactants})$
$\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = 2 - (1 + 3) = 2 - 4 = -2$

The relationship between change in enthalpy ($\Delta \text{H}$) and change in internal energy ($\Delta \text{U}$) is given by:
$\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U} + \Delta \text{n}_\text{g}\text{RT}$

Substituting the value of $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}$, we get:
$\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U} - 2\text{RT}$

Answer: $\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U} - 2\text{RT}$

111941.sol:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because tert-butyl carbocation is a $3^{\circ}$ carbocation and is more stable than isopropyl carbocation, which is a $2^{\circ}$ carbocation.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

113900.subject: Chemistry
113900.text:
The amount of urea ($\mathrm{NH_2CONH_2}$) required to prepare $500\text{ mL}$ of a decimolar aqueous solution is :
(Molar mass of urea : $60\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
113900.sol:
A decimolar solution means the molarity is $0.1\text{ M}$.

The formula for molarity ($\mathrm{M}$) is:
$\mathrm{M} = \dfrac{w \times 1000}{M_w \times V}$

Where:
$w = \text{mass of solute}$
$M_w = \text{molar mass of urea} = 60\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
$V = \text{volume of solution in mL} = 500\text{ mL}$

Substituting the values:
$0.1 = \dfrac{w \times 1000}{60 \times 500}$

$0.1 = \dfrac{w \times 2}{60}$

$w = \dfrac{0.1 \times 60}{2} = 3.0\text{ g}$

Thus, $3.0\text{ g}$ of urea is required.

Answer: $3.0\text{ g}$

114886.text: For a zero order reaction, the rate constant is $1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol L}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$. If the half-life of the reaction is $100 \text{ s}$, what is the initial concentration of the reactant?
114886.sol:
For a zero order reaction, the half-life is given by:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$

Rearranging for initial concentration $[A]_0$:

$[A]_0 = 2 \times k \times t_{1/2}$

Substituting the given values:

$[A]_0 = 2 \times (1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol L}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}) \times 100 \text{ s}$

$[A]_0 = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 = 0.30 \text{ M}$

Answer: $0.30 \text{ M}$

117733.subject: Chemistry
117733.text: Which of the following structural conditions is strictly necessary for a coordination compound to exhibit coordination isomerism?
options: The presence of at least one ambidentate ligand in the coordination sphere
A counter ion outside the coordination sphere that can act as a potential ligand
Both the cationic and anionic entities of the salt must be complex ions
The presence of solvent molecules that can interchange with ligands in the coordination sphere
117733.sol:
Coordination isomerism occurs when there is an interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions present in a complex.

For this interchange to be possible, the coordination compound must consist of both a complex cation and a complex anion. If only one part is a complex ion and the other is a simple ion, coordination isomerism cannot occur.

The presence of an ambidentate ligand leads to linkage isomerism. A counter ion acting as a potential ligand leads to ionization isomerism. The interchange of solvent molecules leads to solvate isomerism.

Answer: Both the cationic and anionic entities of the salt must be complex ions

125643.subject: Botany
125643.text: Which of the following acts as the primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor in the mesophyll cells of Maize?
125643.sol:
Maize is a $\text{C}_4$ plant. In the $\text{C}_4$ pathway (Hatch-Slack pathway), the primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule, Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP), which is present in the mesophyll cells. The enzyme responsible for this fixation is PEP carboxylase (PEPcase).

Ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) is the primary acceptor in $\text{C}_3$ plants. Oxaloacetic acid is the first stable product of $\text{C}_4$ plants, not the acceptor. 3-Phosphoglyceric acid is the first stable product in $\text{C}_3$ plants.

Answer: Phosphoenol pyruvate

Match List-I with List-II regarding polysaccharides and their characteristics.

List-IList-II
(A) Inulin(I) Forms helical secondary structures to hold iodine

126725.text: When an inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme by competing for the active site, the phenomenon is known as competitive inhibition. Which of the following is a classic example of this type of inhibition?
options: Inhibition of cytochrome oxidase by cyanide
Inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate
Inhibition of malonate dehydrogenase by succinate
126725.sol:
The question describes competitive inhibition, where the inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site due to structural similarity.

According to NCERT, a classic example of competitive inhibition is the inhibition of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase by malonate. Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in its molecular structure.

Option 1 is incorrect because cyanide is a non-competitive inhibitor of cytochrome oxidase.

Option 2 is incorrect because glucose-6-phosphate causes feedback inhibition of hexokinase.

Option 4 is incorrect because it incorrectly swaps the roles of the substrate (succinate) and the inhibitor (malonate).

Answer: Inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate

127782.subject: Botany
127782.text:
Read the following statements regarding decomposition and its regulating factors:
A. Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process.
B. The rate of decomposition is quicker if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin.
C. Humus is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
D. Warm and moist environment inhibit decomposition whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis favour it.
E. By the process of leaching, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
127782.sol:
Statement A is correct as decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process.

Statement B is incorrect because the decomposition rate is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker if it is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars.

Statement C is correct as humus is a dark-coloured, amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes at an extremely slow rate.

Statement D is incorrect because a warm and moist environment favours decomposition, whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit it, resulting in the buildup of organic materials.

Statement E is correct as leaching causes water-soluble inorganic nutrients to seep into the soil horizon and precipitate as unavailable salts.

Therefore, only statements A, C, and E are correct.

Answer: A, C and E only

127884.subject: Zoology
127884.text: How many types of tissues does each organ in our body contain?
options: One or more types of tissues
127884.sol:
.

The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful study that the complexity in organ and organ systems displays certain discernable trend. This discernable trend is called evolutionary trend (You will study the details in class XII). In this chapter, you are being introduced to morphology and anatomy of frog. Morphology refers to study of form or externally visible features. In the case of plants or microbes, the term morphology precisely means only this. In case of animals this refers to the external appearance of the organs or parts of the body. The word anatomy conventionally is used for the study of morphology of internal organs in the animals. You will learn the morphology and anatomy of frog representing vertebrates

128372.subject: Zoology
128372.text: What is the main hormone produced by Leydig cells in male individuals?
128372.sol: A pair of testis is present in the scrotal sac (outside abdomen) of male individuals (Figure 19.1). Testis performs dual functions as a primary sex organ as well as an endocrine gland. Testis is composed of seminiferous tubules and stromal or interstitial tissue. The Leydig cells or interstitial cells, which are present in the intertubular spaces produce a group of hormones called androgens mainly testosterone. Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs like epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland, urethra etc. These hormones stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, low pitch of voice etc. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of spermatogenesis (formation of spermatozoa). Androgens act on the central neural system and influence the male sexual behaviour (libido). These hormones produce anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.

128923.subject: Zoology
128923.text: What is the blood pumped by the right ventricle called?
128923.sol: The blood pumped by the right ventricle enters the pulmonary artery, whereas the left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta. The deoxygenated blood pumped into the pulmonary artery is passed on to the lungs from where the oxygenated blood is carried by the pulmonary veins into the left atrium. This pathway constitutes the pulmonary circulation. The oxygenated blood entering the aorta is carried by a network of arteries, arterioles and capillaries to the tissues from where the deoxygenated blood is collected by a system of venules, veins and vena cava and emptied into the right atrium. This is the systemic circulation (Figure 15.4). The systemic circulation provides nutrients, O2 and other essential substances to the tissues and takes CO2 and other harmful substances away for elimination.
